target_customer: Developers, fintechs and businesses that embed stock and crypto investing into their apps, and algorithmic traders
problem: Building a brokerage is slow and heavily regulated. Developers and algo traders lacked a commission free, API first way to trade stocks.
business_model: Usage based brokerage API infrastructure, payment for order flow and fees from partners

founders.name: Yoshi Yokokawa
previous_startups: Other tech startups focused on deep learning and enterprise (names not given on YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page: VP in securitized products at Lehman and Nomura, then a full time day trader.

founders.name: Hitoshi Harada
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder and CTO on the YC page, no background given.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed a real brokerage stack with clearing, order routing, market data and an API, plus FINRA broker dealer compliance, which is hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Licenses (broker dealer, later crypto and Japan entities) and deep integrations by partners made copying slow and expensive.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the wedge. Alpaca grew by adding crypto, international entities (AlpacaJapan acquired July 2022) and partners such as SBI.

market_need_then: Commission free trading and developer demand for trading APIs were rising in 2018 and 2019. Alpaca reported over 1 billion dollars in transactions after about one year (Crowdfund Insider, November 2019).

branding.name_origin: The company says it chose Alpaca because alpacas felt approachable, lively, memorable, cute and funny (company About page, found via search).

identity.logo: Alpaca animal logo (listed on Brandfetch, no design story found)

branding.brand_signature: Alpaca animal as a friendly face for a regulated brokerage
branding.community_and_virality: Open source and developer community, paper trading sandbox and open office hours (company pages). No independent press on the brand found.

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable animal name in a dry category and an active developer community, but evidence of brand driven growth is only the company's own pages.

outcome_analysis: Alpaca is a growth stage company with about 150 staff. It raised a 6 million dollar seed in 2019, a 10 million dollar Series A in 2020, a 50 million dollar Series B in 2021 and a 52 million dollar Series C in 2025, plus a 15 million dollar SBI investment in 2023. Its API first positioning, licenses and international expansion (AlpacaJapan in 2022) drove growth. No failure signals were found in the sources.
notes: Series B blog states total raised of 72 million dollars while itemized rounds are 16 million, so earlier rounds exist (a search summary of Crowdfund Insider mentions 5.8 million from earlier investors including Y Combinator). Crowdfund Insider page returned 403, so the seed details come from the search summary. Series A investor shown is the lead stated by the Series B post. Series C investor list is from search summary and aggregators, not fully verified. A 150 million dollar Series D in January 2026 and a Tencent 2024 round appear only on aggregators and are not recorded. The 2023 SBI investment is a convertible note per the YC page. Competitors (Interactive Brokers, Tradier, Robinhood) appeared only in an undated review so none are listed. Founder education not found. No negative outcome news found.
